reply_text:
*I’d hold the merge.* Reviewed `http-retries` (`b04b610`) against `main` (`5f9be03`). Three findings:

1. *High — `timeoutMs: 0` no longer disables timeouts* — `src/http.js:11`
   Changing `??` to `||` turns explicit `0` into the 10-second default. This affects the existing nightly export caller (`src/export.js:4`), which deliberately disables timeouts. Confirmed: main schedules no timer; this branch schedules 10,000 ms. Restore nullish defaulting and add a zero-timeout regression test.

2. *High — automatic retries can duplicate writes* — `src/http.js:30–33`
   Retries apply to every HTTP method by default, including POST. A server can commit a write and still return 503; replaying it can repeat the operation. A local-server reproduction produced *two writes from one `request()` call*. Restrict automatic retries to safe/idempotent operations, with explicit opt-in for writes protected by an idempotency mechanism.

3. *Medium — discarded retry responses aren’t released* — `src/http.js:32–33`
   Before retrying, the client neither consumes nor cancels the previous response body. Confirmed both discarded 503 bodies remained unread and uncancelled. With real fetch responses, this can retain connections/resources and exhaust the pool under load. Release each discarded body before the next attempt; leave the final returned response untouched.

*Validation:* All three existing tests pass, but they miss these cases. Ran additional in-memory/local-server reproductions. No files changed.
